name: MAX713CSE+T
title: NiCd/NiMH battery fast-charge controllers
summary: The MAX712 and MAX713 are linear fast-charge controllers for 1 to 16 series NiCd or NiMH cells. They drive an external PNP pass transistor, regulate charge current through a low-side sense resistor, and end fast charge on voltage slope, battery temperature or a timer, then fall back to a trickle rate. The MAX712 stops on zero voltage slope and the MAX713 on a negative slope; nothing else separates them. An internal 5 V shunt regulator runs the chip from the DC source, and with that source gone the battery drain is 5 µA at most.

pins.name: VLIMIT
pins.function: Cell voltage ceiling. BATT+ to BATT- is held at or below VLIMIT times the programmed cell count. Keep it at 2.5 V or lower; for normal use it is tied to REF.

pins.name: PGM0
pins.function: Cell-count strap, with PGM1: each is tied to V+, REF or BATT- or left open, giving 1 to 16 cells (Table 2). Above 11 cells the BATT+ voltage needs external limiting when DC IN is absent. A battery with more or fewer cells than programmed can defeat voltage-slope termination.

pins.name: THI
pins.function: Over-temperature threshold. Fast charge stops when TEMP rises past THI.

pins.name: TLO
pins.function: Under-temperature threshold. If TEMP is below TLO at power-on, fast charge waits until TEMP climbs above TLO.

pins.name: TEMP
pins.function: Thermistor sense input: a voltage that tracks battery temperature.

pins.name: FASTCHG
pins.function: Active-low fast-charge status. Sinks current during fast charge and stops sinking when the part drops to trickle charge.

pins.name: PGM2
pins.function: Fast-charge timeout strap, with PGM3: V+, REF, BATT- or open, giving 22 to 264 min and turning voltage-slope termination on or off (Table 3).

pins.name: PGM3
pins.function: Timeout strap with PGM2 (Table 3); also sets the ratio of fast to trickle current (Table 5).

pins.name: CC
pins.function: Compensation node of the constant-current loop; C2 goes from CC to BATT-.

pins.name: BATT-
pins.function: Battery negative terminal and the reference for every specified voltage.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: System ground. The sense resistor sits between BATT- and GND and measures battery current.

pins.name: DRV
pins.function: Current-sink output that drives the base of the external PNP pass transistor.

pins.name: V+
pins.function: Shunt-regulated supply, held at 5 V above BATT-; the shunt current is what powers the chip.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: Linear charger with the battery's load hung across it. The wall cube's positive output is DC IN, held up by a 10 µF capacitor. Q1, a 2N6109 PNP, passes charge current from DC IN through D1 (1N4001) to the battery; DRV sinks Q1's base current, R2 (150 Ω) pulls the base up to DC IN and C4 (0.01 µF) sits across R2. R1 feeds the V+ shunt regulator, bypassed by C1 (1 µF) to BATT-; THI is tied to V+. VLIMIT is tied to REF, and R3 (68 kΩ) with R4 (22 kΩ) divides REF down to TEMP: the fixed divider used in place of thermistors when temperature cutoff is off. TLO goes to BATT-, so there is no cold inhibit. C2 (0.01 µF) compensates the current loop from CC to BATT-. RSENSE runs from the battery's negative terminal (BATT-) to GND, and the load and C3 (10 µF) are connected from BATT+ to GND.

parts.note: DC source; lowest output above 6 V and 1.5 V over the highest battery voltage

circuits.title: Charging example: 3 NiMH AA cells at 1 A
circuits.description: The typical operating circuit with the thermistor network of the temperature-comparator circuit, as used to charge three 1000 mAh Gold Peak GP1000AAH NiMH cells at 1 A from a Sony AC-190 adapter (9 VDC, 800 mA). RSENSE is 0.25 Ω, so the fast-charge current is 1 A; R1 is 200 Ω. PGM0 to V+ and PGM1 to REF set 3 cells; PGM2 and PGM3 to REF set a 90 min timeout with voltage-slope termination on. VLIMIT goes to REF. R3 (10 kΩ) and R4 (15 kΩ) divide REF to set THI, with 0.022 µF on THI; thermistor T1, on the battery, runs from REF to TEMP and T2, at ambient, from TEMP to BATT-, with 1 µF on TEMP. R5 and T3 are left out and TLO is tied to BATT-.

parts.note: NTC thermistor in thermal contact with the battery

notes: Results with each part are the curves '3 NiMH cells charged with MAX712' and 'NiMH cells charged with MAX713'.

circuits.title: DRV pin cascode connection
circuits.description: Partial circuit for a DC IN above 20 V, or to take dissipation off the chip in linear mode. A 2N3904 NPN sits between DRV and the base of the pass transistor Q1: its emitter on DRV, its collector on Q1's base, and its base on V+, so DRV never sees the full DC IN voltage. R1 from DC IN feeds V+; R2 pulls Q1's base to DC IN. Q1's collector feeds the battery through D1.

circuits.title: Reduction of trickle current for NiMH batteries (linear mode)
circuits.description: Partial circuit that takes the trickle current below C/16. FASTCHG, pulled up to V+ by 10 kΩ, drives NPN Q2 through another 10 kΩ. During fast charge FASTCHG is low and Q2 is off. In trickle charge FASTCHG releases, Q2 turns on and R7 carries part of the regulated trickle current from the pass-transistor side of D1 round the battery to its negative terminal, so less of it flows in the cells. R7 comes from the R7 equation.

circuits.title: Temperature comparators
circuits.description: Partial circuit: the thermistor network. T1, in thermal contact with the battery, runs from REF to TEMP, and T2, at ambient, from TEMP to BATT-, so TEMP sits near 1 V when battery and ambient match and rises as the battery warms. R3 and R4 divide REF to set THI, with 0.022 µF on THI. R5 from REF and ambient thermistor T3 to BATT- set TLO, with 0.022 µF on TLO, and 1 µF filters TEMP. T1 and T2 are the same model. For an absolute-temperature cutoff, T2 and T3 can be fixed resistors.

parts.note: in thermal contact with the battery

notes: Resistances in the network are chosen between 10 kΩ and 500 kΩ.

circuits.title: Alternative temperature comparator configuration
circuits.description: Partial circuit for packs whose own thermistor is tied to the pack's negative terminal. The battery thermistor T1 runs from THI to BATT-, under ambient thermistor T2 from REF. R3 and R4 divide REF to set TEMP, with 1 µF on TEMP. R5 from REF and ambient thermistor T3 to BATT- set TLO. THI and TLO each carry 0.022 µF. T2 and T3 can be fixed resistors for an absolute-temperature cutoff.

parts.note: in thermal contact with the battery

notes: Resistances in the network are chosen between 10 kΩ and 500 kΩ.

circuits.title: Cascoding to accommodate high cell counts for linear-mode circuits
circuits.description: Partial circuit for more than 11 cells, which keeps BATT+ inside its unpowered rating when DC IN is absent. NPN Q2 sits between the battery's positive terminal (collector) and BATT+ (emitter), its base fed from DC IN through 33 kΩ. DRV drives the base of pass transistor Q1 through 500 Ω, R2 (150 Ω) pulls that base up to DC IN, and Q1 charges the battery through D1.

circuits.title: Shunting RSENSE for efficiency improvement
circuits.description: Partial circuit that bypasses the sense resistor while the charger is unpowered, for stacks of more than 4 cells. A low-on-resistance logic-level N-channel MOSFET sits across RSENSE, drain on the battery's negative terminal and source on GND. Its gate is pulled up to the battery's positive side by 100 kΩ, so it conducts when the charger is off. An NPN whose base is fed from V+ through 100 kΩ pulls the gate to GND while V+ is up, leaving RSENSE in circuit during charging.

circuits.title: Logic-level status outputs
circuits.description: Two logic signals for a host. V+ serves directly as a power flag: 0 V with no input, 5 V with the charger powered. FASTCHG, pulled up to the host's VCC by 10 kΩ, reads 0 V during fast charge and VCC in trickle charge or with no power.

parts.value: power status: 0 V no power, 5 V power
charge status: 0 V fast, VCC trickle or no power

circuits.title: LED connection for status outputs
circuits.description: Two indicator LEDs in one string. From DC IN, R1 feeds the charge-power LED into V+, so it lights whenever the shunt regulator draws current. From V+, a resistor of 470 Ω or more feeds the fast-charge LED into FASTCHG, which lights it only while FASTCHG sinks current during fast charge.

operation.text: The part is always either fast charging or trickle charging. It forces a constant current into the battery and watches three things to decide when it is full: the slope of battery voltage, battery temperature and elapsed time. Any one of them ends fast charge.

With no input the chip draws negligible current from the battery. When DC IN arrives, power-on reset holds trickle charge; when reset clears, fast charge begins provided the battery voltage divided by the cell count is above the 0.4 V undervoltage lockout. A negative voltage slope then ends fast charge, and on removal of input the drain falls back to negligible.
A pack too cold for fast charge stays in trickle charge until it warms to a safe temperature; fast charge then starts, and ends when the temperature passes the THI limit.

With no battery, the output is regulated at VLIMIT times the cell count. When a battery is inserted the part sees current flow into it and goes to fast charge, then to trickle once full. If the battery is pulled out it stays in trickle and returns to regulating the output voltage.

The source's lowest output, ripple included, must be above 6 V and at least 1.5 V higher than the highest battery voltage during charge. Correct fast-charge termination depends on meeting this. Plain wall cubes (transformer, bridge, capacitor) have large 120 Hz ripple, so the low point of the ripple at full load is what counts. Pack voltage during fast charge can reach 1.9 V per cell, and the 1.5 V margin covers Q1, D1 and RSENSE.

Pick termination per Table 1 and the cell manufacturer's limits; choose the rate (C/4 is the slowest, since the longest timeout is 264 min); set the cell count with PGM0/PGM1 and recheck it whenever the cell count changes; choose the DC source; work out Q1 and D1 dissipation; size R1 for 5 to 20 mA into V+; choose RSENSE; set the straps before power is applied. The timeout is set to 1.5 to 2 times the expected charge time, for example 3 or 4 hours at C/2.

The voltage-slope converter sees battery voltage divided by the programmed cell count, and that must stay between 1.4 V and 1.9 V. A battery with more or fewer cells than programmed can push it out of range and disable voltage-slope termination.

With no wall cube the part is idle and takes 5 µA at most from the battery; D1 blocks current back into DRV. On connection, C1 charges through R1 (or a current-limiting diode) to 5 V, the shunt regulator starts sinking current to hold V+ at 5 V, and fast charge begins. R1 or the limiting part must pass at least 5 mA at the lowest DC IN. Above 20 V of DC IN, a cascode transistor in series with DRV keeps DRV within its rating. Shunt current and DRV sink current both heat the chip, and their sum must stay inside the package dissipation limit.

Fast charge begins at power-up with a battery already fitted, when battery current is detected (GND below BATT-), TEMP lies between TLO and THI, and the cell voltage is above the lockout; or at battery insertion under the same temperature and voltage conditions.
In fast charge the loop holds BATT- to GND at 250 mV: DRV sinks more current when the sense voltage is below 250 mV and less when it is above. RSENSE alone therefore sets the fast-charge current.

Trickle current is set by raising the gain of the current-sense amplifier, which lowers the regulated sense voltage. With IFAST at C/2, C, 2C or 4C and PGM3 matched per Table 5, the trickle is C/16; other fast rates give a trickle that is not exactly C/16.

Two Panasonic P-50AA 500 mAh AA NiCd cells at C/3, 264 min timeout, negative-slope cutoff on and a 6 V minimum input: MAX713 with PGM0 = V+, PGM1 = open, PGM2 = BATT-, PGM3 = BATT-, RSENSE = 1.5 Ω (IFAST = 167 mA) and R1 = 200 Ω. With PGM3 on BATT-, the trickle sense voltage is 31.3 mV, a current of 20.7 mA, which is C/25 rather than C/16.

One loop controls both the BATT+ to BATT- voltage and the battery current: DRV sink current is cut back when the output exceeds VLIMIT times the cell count or the battery current exceeds its programmed value. In a linear charger this lets the battery be removed without interrupting the load while the charger is powered, and, with the load wired as in the typical circuit, battery current stays regulated whatever the load draws, as long as the source can supply both.

With VLIMIT below 2.5 V, BATT+ is limited to VLIMIT times the programmed cell count. VLIMIT belongs between 1.9 V and 2.5 V; set below the highest cell voltage it can stop fast charge from terminating properly. Tying VLIMIT to REF is the normal choice. With no battery the part does not regulate current; it holds BATT+ at that maximum voltage.
The output filter capacitor stabilises the voltage loop. A large one is needed only when the charger has to supply the load with no battery fitted; then it is sized by the COUT equation.

C2 sets the current-loop bandwidth, which must stay below the PNP's own pole, found as a single-pole fT/B0 response from its data. The DRV current-voltage product heats the chip; the cascode connection reduces it.

The internal converter resolves 2.5 mV. Each decision cycle is two tA intervals (21 s to 168 s, Table 3), each followed by a 5 ms battery-voltage conversion; the two readings are compared, and if fast charge does not end the cycle starts again. A MAX712 ends fast charge when the reading has not changed; a MAX713 ends it when the reading has fallen by 2.5 mV per cell or more. The two parts differ in nothing else.

Negative-coefficient thermistors sense over- and under-temperature. With T1 and T2 the same model, TEMP reads 1 V above BATT- with battery and surroundings at one temperature. Once TEMP climbs past THI, fast charge stops for good; a later drop below THI does not restart it. If TLO is above TEMP at start-up, fast charge waits until TEMP exceeds TLO. Cold inhibit is off with TLO tied to BATT- and R5, T3 and the TLO capacitor left out. Temperature cutoff is off altogether with THI tied to V+, TLO tied to BATT-, the thermistor network (T1 to T3, R3 to R5 and their capacitors) left out, and a 68 kΩ / 22 kΩ divider from REF to TEMP to BATT-.

operation.topic: Thermistor on the pack's negative terminal
operation.text: Packs with a built-in thermistor tied to the negative terminal use the alternative comparator network. T2 and T3 can be fixed resistors when an absolute-temperature cutoff is acceptable. All network resistances are chosen between 10 kΩ and 500 kΩ.

Three Gold Peak GP1000AAH 1000 mAh NiMH AA cells charged at 1 A with each part, on the typical circuit with the temperature-comparator thermistors: Sony AC-190 (9 VDC, 800 mA) input; PGM0 = V+, PGM1 = REF, PGM2 = REF, PGM3 = REF; R1 = 200 Ω, R2 = 150 Ω, RSENSE = 0.25 Ω; C1 = 1 µF, C2 = 0.01 µF, C3 = 10 µF, VLIMIT = REF; R3 = 10 kΩ, R4 = 15 kΩ; T1 and T2 Alpha Sensors 14A1002; R5 and T3 omitted, TLO = BATT-.

BATT+ is rated higher when the part is powered. Above 11 cells the BATT+ voltage has to be limited by external parts while DC IN is absent, for example with the cascode transistor of the high-cell-count circuit.

RSENSE costs a little efficiency while the battery is in use, which matters only when RSENSE is large next to the stack's internal resistance. A MOSFET can short RSENSE whenever the charger is unpowered.
V+ and FASTCHG give charger status as logic levels, or can drive LEDs for charge power and fast charge.
Inside, each of PGM0 to PGM3 is tied to V+ by 100 kΩ and to REF by 100 kΩ.
